narratives.title: Geopolitical Escalation Drives Risk-Off
narratives.summary: Capital is fleeing risk assets as multi-front conflicts (Iran, Israel, Ukraine) escalate beyond controlled tit-for-tat, with actual kinetic exchanges and supply chain threats. The market consensus underestimates the persistence and breadth of these conflicts, as evidenced by the Hormuz blockade, Apache shootdown, and deep strikes into Russia.
narratives.trade_implication: Short equities (S&P 500) and long volatility (VIX futures) as algorithmic stop-loss cascades and genuine repricing of geopolitical risk premium unfold.

narratives.title: Energy Supply Disruption Is Structural
narratives.summary: Capital is rotating into energy commodities as the Hormuz blockade persists through Q3 2026 per EIA, with Kuwait seeking pipeline bypasses and the US SPR release signaling bullish supply pre-positioning. The market misreads these as bearish, but actual physical constraints and delayed recovery support higher oil prices.
narratives.trade_implication: Long WTI crude oil futures and energy sector ETFs (XLE), with a target of $95+ as blockade bites and diplomatic off-ramps remain uncertain.

narratives.title: Crypto Decoupling From Risk Assets
narratives.summary: Despite BTC's crash, capital flows show institutional accumulation (MicroStrategy buying the dip, whales holding) and retail dip-buying, suggesting crypto is experiencing macro risk-off contagion rather than a crypto-specific crisis. This divergence from equities indicates a potential decoupling narrative as fundamentals remain intact.
narratives.trade_implication: Accumulate Bitcoin (BTC) spot or futures on dips, targeting a reversion to $75K+ as macro fears subside and institutional demand absorbs selling pressure.
